beat_count_note: Bhajan song sheets often give only a beat count, e.g. 'Taal (5,6,7,8)'. These counts are the beats the singer/clapper feels per cycle, not the number of tabla matras, so score labels at the beat-count level first and treat names as candidates: 8 -> keherwa (Hindustani) / adi (Carnatic) - also bhajani theka and dhumali; a 16-beat teentaal/tilwada/addha is usually felt as 8+8. 6 -> dadra (Hindustani) / tisra-nadai or rupakam (Carnatic light music) - also khemta; a fast 6 is often notated 3. 7 -> rupak (Hindustani) / misra chapu (Carnatic, 3+2+2) - also tisra triputa. 5 -> khanda chapu (Carnatic, 2+3); jhaptaal (10 = 2+3+2+3) is half-cycle-equivalent only loosely (it is really 10). Counts related by a factor of 2 (3/6/12, 4/8/16, 5/10, 7/14) describe the same metre at a different counting level and should be scored as compatible but not equal.

symbols.I<n>: laghu of n counts (clap + finger counts)

taals.name: keherwa
taals.equivalents: adi tala (Carnatic light music); chatusra eka x2
taals.feel: The default bhajan, folk and film-song taal; steady 4-beat pulse.

taals.name: dadra
taals.theka_note: Also commonly 'dha dhin na | na tin na'.
taals.equivalents: tisra nadai / tisra eka x2 and rupakam (6 aksharas) in Carnatic light music
taals.feel: Lilting 6-beat taal of bhajans, ghazals, lullabies and folk songs.

taals.name: rupak
taals.equivalents: misra chapu (3+2+2) - near-identical grouping; tisra triputa (3+2+2)
taals.feel: Asymmetric 7 that starts on the empty (khali) beat; light classical, bhajans, film songs.

taals.name: jhaptaal
taals.equivalents: khanda chapu x2 (2+3 twice) in feel; Carnatic jhampa (7+1+2) and matya (4+2+4) share only the count
taals.feel: Medium-tempo classical and semi-classical; bhajans set in 'half' groupings of 5.

taals.name: teentaal
taals.equivalents: adi tala in 2-kalai (16 counts) / adi counted at double speed
taals.feel: The most common classical taal; in bhajans usually heard as two cycles of a 4/4 feel.

taals.name: ektaal
taals.western: 12/8 or 6/4 (six pairs); drut ektaal is felt as 4 groups of 3
taals.equivalents: no standard Carnatic equivalent (12 counts; loosely tisra-nadai adi or 3 x chatusra eka)
taals.feel: Vilambit and drut khayal; occasionally slow devotional pieces.

taals.name: deepchandi
taals.western: 14/8 (3+4+3+4), often felt as 7/4 or two bars of 7/8
taals.equivalents: Carnatic dhruva/ata share the count only; in light music close to misra chapu x2
taals.feel: Thumri, dadra-style light classical, Holi and devotional songs; lilting long-short swing.

taals.name: chanchar
taals.theka_note: No single standard theka: many treat chanchar as a folk/light form of deepchandi (same 3+4+3+4 cycle); bol sets vary by region and gharana.
taals.equivalents: same as deepchandi
taals.feel: Folk and light-classical (Punjabi, Rajasthani, Holi songs); faster and bouncier than deepchandi.

taals.name: bhajanitheka
taals.theka_note: An 8-beat dholak/pakhawaj theka of Marathi and North-Indian bhajan singing; its bols vary by region and player, so no single standard theka is given.
taals.western: 4/4 with a strong triplet/swung feel (often transcribed 12/8)
taals.equivalents: keherwa (same count); adi in tisra nadai feel
taals.feel: Driving, swung 8 of community bhajan and kirtan singing, usually with manjira/kartal.

taals.name: khemta
taals.theka_note: Bengali/folk 6-beat taal; bols vary by region and player (sometimes counted as 12), so no single standard theka is given.
taals.equivalents: dadra (same count); tisra nadai in Carnatic light music
taals.feel: Fast, swinging 6 of Bengali folk, kirtan and light songs.

taals.name: dhumali
taals.theka_note: 8-beat light/devotional taal close to keherwa; thekas vary by gharana and region, so none is asserted.
taals.equivalents: keherwa; adi (light music)
taals.feel: Light devotional, bhajan and qawwali-style accompaniment with syncopated accents.

taals.name: addha
taals.theka_note: Commonly cited form; addha / sitarkhani / punjabi thekas vary by gharana.
taals.equivalents: teentaal (same structure); adi 2-kalai
taals.feel: Swung 16 for thumri, tappa, bhajans and qawwali.

taals.name: tilwada
taals.equivalents: teentaal (same structure); adi 2-kalai
taals.feel: Very slow (vilambit) khayal accompaniment.

taals.name: jhoomra
taals.equivalents: deepchandi (same grouping, different theka); Carnatic dhruva/ata by count only
taals.feel: Very slow (vilambit) khayal; distinguished from deepchandi by its dense 'tirakita' theka.

taals.name: chautaal
taals.theka_note: Pakhawaj theka.
taals.equivalents: ektaal (same count and divisions)
taals.feel: Dhrupad and temple/haveli devotional singing on pakhawaj.

taals.name: dhamar
taals.theka_note: Pakhawaj theka.
taals.equivalents: Carnatic ata/dhruva by count only
taals.feel: Dhrupad-style Holi (hori) compositions.

taals.name: sooltaal
taals.theka_note: Pakhawaj theka.
taals.equivalents: jhaptaal (count only); Carnatic matya/jhampa by count only
taals.feel: Dhrupad; occasionally temple bhajans.

taals.name: adi
taals.clap_wave: clap, pinky, ring, middle | clap, wave | clap, wave
taals.theka_note: Carnatic talas have no fixed theka; the mridangam improvises within the tala using sollukattu patterns, so no standard bol sequence is given.
taals.western: 4/4 (8 beats = one 8/8 bar or two 4/4 bars; 2-kalai adi = 16)
taals.equivalents: keherwa (light music); teentaal for 2-kalai adi
taals.feel: The default Carnatic tala for kritis and most South-Indian bhajans.

taals.name: rupakam
taals.clap_wave: clap, wave | clap, pinky, ring, middle
taals.theka_note: Carnatic talas have no fixed theka; the mridangam improvises within the tala using sollukattu patterns, so no standard bol sequence is given. In practice it is often counted as 3 beats (6 aksharas at 2 per beat), especially in light music.
taals.equivalents: dadra (6) in light music; NOT Hindustani rupak (7)
taals.feel: Common in kritis and devotional songs; a 3-feel in light music.

taals.name: mishrachapu
taals.clap_wave: wave (or silent) on 1, clap on 4, clap on 6 - 'ta ki ta | ta ka | dhi mi'
taals.theka_note: Solkattu counting syllables, not a drum theka; mridangam patterns vary.
taals.equivalents: rupak (Hindustani, 3+2+2, also starting on an unaccented beat)
taals.feel: Lilting 7 used for padams, devotional songs and many bhajans.

taals.name: khandachapu
taals.clap_wave: clap on 1 and 3 - 'ta ka | ta ki ta'
taals.theka_note: Solkattu counting syllables, not a drum theka.
taals.equivalents: jhaptaal (10 = 2+3+2+3) is two cycles of the same grouping
taals.feel: Brisk 5 used in devotional songs, tillanas and javalis.

taals.name: tisraeka
taals.theka_note: Carnatic talas have no fixed theka; the mridangam improvises within the tala using sollukattu patterns, so no standard bol sequence is given.
taals.equivalents: dadra counted in 3 (dadra = 2 cycles)
taals.feel: Simple triple metre; light and devotional songs.

taals.name: tisranadaiadi
taals.vibhag: I4 O O (each beat subdivided in 3)
taals.clap_wave: as adi: clap, pinky, ring, middle | clap, wave | clap, wave - with three pulses per beat
taals.theka_note: Carnatic talas have no fixed theka; the mridangam improvises within the tala using sollukattu patterns, so no standard bol sequence is given.
taals.western: 12/8 (8 beats x 3 = 24 pulses = two bars of 12/8)
taals.equivalents: dadra / khemta feel (6-feel) and bhajani theka (swung 8)
taals.feel: Triplet-feel adi; what many 'Taal 6' South-Indian bhajans actually use.

taals.name: chatusraeka
taals.theka_note: Carnatic talas have no fixed theka; the mridangam improvises within the tala using sollukattu patterns, so no standard bol sequence is given.
taals.equivalents: half a keherwa cycle
taals.feel: Simple duple metre; fast pieces, tillanas, devotional songs.

taals.name: jhampa
taals.clap_wave: clap + 6 finger counts | clap (anudrutam) | clap, wave
taals.theka_note: Carnatic talas have no fixed theka; the mridangam improvises within the tala using sollukattu patterns, so no standard bol sequence is given.
taals.equivalents: jhaptaal by count only (grouping differs: 2+3+2+3)
taals.feel: Rare in light music; used in some kritis and dasa padas (Purandara Dasa 'jhampe').

taals.name: triputa
taals.jati: tisra (default; adi is the chatusra form)
taals.clap_wave: clap, pinky, ring | clap, wave | clap, wave
taals.theka_note: Carnatic talas have no fixed theka; the mridangam improvises within the tala using sollukattu patterns, so no standard bol sequence is given.
taals.equivalents: rupak / misra chapu (same 3+2+2 grouping)
taals.feel: Used in some kritis and dasa padas; same grouping as misra chapu but counted with angas.

taals.name: ata
taals.clap_wave: clap + 4 counts | clap + 4 counts | clap, wave | clap, wave
taals.theka_note: Carnatic talas have no fixed theka; the mridangam improvises within the tala using sollukattu patterns, so no standard bol sequence is given.
taals.equivalents: Hindustani 14-beat taals (deepchandi, dhamar) by count only
taals.feel: Slow varnams and some dasa padas.

taals.name: dhruva
taals.clap_wave: clap + 3 counts | clap, wave | clap + 3 counts | clap + 3 counts
taals.theka_note: Carnatic talas have no fixed theka; the mridangam improvises within the tala using sollukattu patterns, so no standard bol sequence is given.
taals.equivalents: Hindustani 14-beat taals by count only
taals.feel: Rare; alankaras and a few compositions.

taals.name: matya
taals.clap_wave: clap + 3 counts | clap, wave | clap + 3 counts
taals.theka_note: Carnatic talas have no fixed theka; the mridangam improvises within the tala using sollukattu patterns, so no standard bol sequence is given.
taals.equivalents: jhaptaal / sooltaal by count only
taals.feel: Rare; alankaras and a few compositions.
